categories.label: Fibre & Textile Making
categories.description:
The places that put on a day of wool: mills with working looms, shops that sell a ticket as well as yarn, and the heritage projects that have taken a fibre strand and run with it.
Short on purpose. Munster has plenty of craft venues and almost none of them are about fibre — a gallery with a textile show twice a decade is not a source, it is a coincidence. The first version of this catalogue was full of arts centres and craft fairs; they are gone, and what is left is the handful of places where wool is actually the subject.

categories.label: Guilds & Networks
categories.description:
The bodies whose whole purpose is this subject: the weavers', spinners' and dyers' guild, the textile networks, the wool council.
These matter more than venues here. A one-off fibre day in Munster is usually organised by two people in a guild rather than programmed by a building, and a guild's news page is the closest thing to a diary the subject has. They are also where a visiting tutor gets announced — which is exactly how a Shetland knitting weekend ends up on an island off Cork.

categories.label: Listings & Notices
categories.description:
The nets: national schemes with searchable programmes, the craft agencies, and the two West Cork papers that covered the flax revival when nobody else did.
A one-off run by two people has no website, so this is where it gets written down — but nearly everything these sources carry is out of scope. They are fetched for the textile strand and nothing else.
